jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11085.txt, EO_11515.txt, EO_12014.txt (sha256 and 15 quoted spans re-verified, unchanged from the blind check)
jobs/later-events/output/CATALOG_INDEX.csv (EO 9586: Amended by EO 10336, 11085, 11515 and nothing later; EO 11085: Amends only)
cruden number EO:11085 and EO:9586 (no later amendment of EO 9586 after EO 11515)
reasoning: The genuine claim differs from the planted one only in the six first_end dates: 1963-02-22 for the two self-executing amendment clauses (sec1-lead, sec2-a-10717) and 1970-03-13 for quoted sections 3 to 6. Those dates match the order's signing date, February 22, 1963, the date of EO 11515, March 13, 1970 (its section 5(2): "By striking out all numbered sections of the order except sections 1 and 2"), and every judgment_reason, the rationale, the member checks and the savings reason. Neither EO 11085 nor EO 11515 has a separate effective-date clause. Hashes and all 15 quoted spans match. Identity is confirmed: EO 11085, The Presidential Medal of Freedom, February 22, 1963, 28 FR 1759, Kennedy. The 12 scopes cover the whole order. Quoted sections 1 and 2(a), (c) and (d) and section 2(b) of the order (existing arrangements continue) are operative. Quoted 2(b) continues as amended by EO 11515 section 5(1). The 1989 OFR codification and the OFR catalog show no amendment of EO 9586 after EO 11515, and cruden finds no later change provision. EO 12014 (1977-10-19) correctly appears as a later event after the Board clauses had ended. Defect 4 of my blind review does not hold on re-examination, and the record should say so. The claim does disclose the 5 U.S.C. 4504 note lead. In the packet that lead is only a snippet, not a held legal-text slice; the dossier says so in its missing list, and the full note text I read was retrieved 2026-11-09, after the claim's 2026-11-06 searches. So "no held current-law text" is accurate in the packet's evidence terms. The note's continued printing of sections 3 to 6 is editorial residue: the note's own credit line lists EO 11515, and the 1989 OFR codification records "Secs. 3-6 removed by EO 11515 of Mar. 13, 1970". It does not affect the ending. A later revision could record that discrepancy, but it is not disqualifying. Continuation of the surviving sections rests, as the claim honestly says, on the absence of any ending in bounded searches. That meets the same standard I applied to the upheld claims in this set. Upheld after reveal.
